fields.status: Work-in-progress native iOS ARM64 port of the GPL KisakCOD engine decompilation. The maintainer's latest status table reports 41/41 engine translation units compiling for arm64-apple-ios, a simulator-verified headless Com_Init milestone, and first engine code executing on iOS. On a physical iPad Pro (M5), the patched DXVK D3D9 frontend through static MoltenVK and a native CAMetalLayer creates a device, passes bit-exact clear readback, and presents successfully; the real player-movement sandbox has only run on a synthetic world. No Call of Duty 4 game frame or playable session is documented, and 32-bit fastfile compatibility remains a major blocker. The repository has no release; latest source push is 2026-07-16.
fields.subtype: iOS/iPadOS research port with on-device D3D9-to-Metal renderer proof; not yet playable

fields.summary: A Rust workspace with an AIR/LLVM IR-to-SPIR-V translator and a separate Metal-shaped runtime over Vulkan. The current README documents compute, render, tessellation, tile, and mesh stages, a Vulkan 1.2 device requirement, typed refusals for unsupported or uncovered inputs, and synthetic public fixtures. Passing spirv-val shows that a module is valid, not that it behaves like Metal. Authored validation compares selected cases against Metal; the private validation corpus is not included in the public repository, so the project does not claim complete compatibility.
